items.title: Mississauga-Raised Netflix Star Helps Nintendo Launch Ocarina of Time Remake in Toronto
items.summary: Mississauga native Maitreyi Ramakrishnan joined Nintendo of Canada in Toronto on Nov. 5 to help launch the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, according to insauga.com. The outlet reported that Ramakrishnan, best known for her breakout role in the Netflix series Never Have I Ever, grew up in Mississauga and attended Meadowvale Secondary School. She told insauga.com she has been a die-hard fan of Nintendo and the Zelda franchise since she was five years old, and called the graphics on the Nintendo Switch especially striking. The outlet noted Ocarina of Time remains one of the franchise's most iconic and culturally influential titles more than 25 years after its original debut. Ramakrishnan graduated from York University in 2025 while continuing to work on film and television projects, insauga.com said. Her most recent role came in Best of the Best, a film about two lifelong friends who join a university Bollywood-fusion dance squad, which premiered on Netflix in September.

items.title: Pearson, United Way and Peel Region Launch $1-Million Program to Place Displaced Auto Workers in Airport Jobs
items.summary: Toronto Pearson, United Way Greater Toronto and Peel Region are putting a combined $1 million into a new workforce program aimed at connecting laid-off workers from Brampton and Mississauga with jobs in the airport's growing employment zone, according to insauga.com. The outlet reported the first phase is a one-year pilot called Peel Gateway for Employment, which is expected to help roughly 200 workers find new career opportunities. Among those targeted are employees affected by layoffs at Stellantis' Brampton assembly plant, along with other workers displaced from the automotive and manufacturing sectors, insauga.com said. The initiative launched Monday at the Unifor Power Centre in Brampton, bringing together representatives from the airport, labour organizations, government and employment agencies, the outlet reported. Rather than steering displaced workers only toward entry-level positions, the program is designed to identify their existing experience and match it to other industries through career coaching, skills development and job placement assistance. The outlet noted the effort could offer a new path for Stellantis employees as the plant's future remains uncertain, with the automaker having announced plans to sell the facility to defence manufacturer Roshel.

items.title: Grey Bruce OPP Charge Mississauga Man After Cannabis Found During Southgate Traffic Stop
items.summary: Grey Bruce OPP have charged a Mississauga man with drug-impaired driving following a traffic stop in the Township of Southgate on Sunday, Nov. 8, according to The Owen Sound Current. The outlet reported that an officer pulled the vehicle over and, while speaking with the driver, noticed evidence of cannabis, prompting an impaired driving investigation. Police arrested the driver, identified as 37-year-old Muhammad Ishfaq of Mississauga, the outlet said. Ishfaq faces three charges: operating a vehicle while impaired by drugs under the Criminal Code, having care or control of a motor vehicle with cannabis readily available under Ontario's Cannabis Control Act, and using plates not authorized for the vehicle under the Highway Traffic Act, according to The Owen Sound Current. The outlet noted the allegations have not been proven in court.

items.title: Pond Dredging Near Swinbourne Drive Pushes Ward 11 Trail Upgrade Into 2027
items.summary: A stormwater management project near Swinbourne Drive in Mississauga's Ward 11 is running into next month, pushing a related pedestrian trail upgrade back to spring 2027, according to Ward 11 Councillor Brad Butt. In a recent update to constituents, Butt said a contractor has been dredging and rehabilitating a pond northwest of Britannia Road West and Silken Laumann Way to manage stormwater, improve flood protection and remove sediment, work that also includes remediation and erosion control. The project began over the summer and is now expected to wrap up by the end of November, Butt said. City staff say the work is part of Mississauga's broader Stormwater Capital Plan, which covers watercourse improvements, storm sewer and drainage upgrades, stormwater management facilities and related studies across the city. According to a 2026 Roads and Stormwater Capital Plan report for Ward 11, projects like this one are identified through the city's stormwater monitoring, evaluation and maintenance programs, as well as recommendations from various studies, and are intended to provide additional flood relief and improve water quality.

items.title: MiWay Riders Face Shifting Bus Stops at City Centre Terminal as Hazel McCallion LRT Work Continues
items.summary: MiWay riders using the City Centre Transit Terminal will see temporary platform closures both inside and outside the building from November 10 to 20, according to the City of Mississauga. The city says the changes are needed to support ongoing construction on the Hazel McCallion LRT line, though access to the terminal itself will remain open during regular operating hours. No buses will serve their usual platforms inside the terminal during this period, and the city says Platform A routes will instead be served from Platform L. Routes will otherwise continue to run on their regular schedules, with only the bus stop locations changing, the city notes. Mississauga is asking riders to plan ahead, watch for posted notices to find their stop, and be patient while travelling through the area as crews work to move people safely through the temporary disruption.

items.title: City Hall to Host Outdoor Remembrance Day Ceremony With Wreaths and a Moment of Silence
items.summary: Mississauga will mark Remembrance Day with an outdoor ceremony at City Hall on November 11, according to the City of Mississauga. The city says the ceremony will pay tribute to both past and present members of the Canadian Armed Forces. Residents are welcome to attend in person, and the program is set to include a moment of silence followed by the laying of wreaths to honour Canadian soldiers and veterans. Those unable to attend in person can instead watch the ceremony through a livestream, the city says. Mississauga also reminds veterans and active Canadian Armed Forces members, whether on regular duty or in reserve, that they can ride MiWay transit for free year round with valid military identification or other proof of service.

items.title: Streetsville Barbershop Owner Turns Walls Into Gallery for Local Artists and His Own Paintings
items.summary: A Streetsville barbershop called Heartbreak Hotel has become more than a place for haircuts, doubling as a showcase for local art and streetwear. According to the Toronto Star, owner Omar Preza, 44, was born in El Salvador and raised in Canada, and built the shop around his lifelong passions for drawing, comic books and street graffiti. The newspaper reported that customers walk in to upbeat Latin and hip-hop music, with painted canvases in thrifted gold frames and custom apparel hanging from industrial pipe racks against black-and-white brick walls. The Star said Heartbreak Hotel began in 2013 as a streetwear clothing brand, with Preza starting to paint around the same time, and today he sells both his original fine art and custom-designed apparel in the shop alongside the haircuts. His work was included in the Art Gallery of Mississauga's 2024-2025 Fourth Annual Juried Show of Visual Arts, according to the paper.

items.title: Newly Elected Mississauga Mayor Faces First Budget Test Over Property Tax Freeze Pledge
items.summary: Mississauga's newly elected mayor, Alvin Tedjo, is preparing to deliver his first budget as residents and local associations watch closely to see whether he can keep his campaign promise of a two-year freeze on the city's portion of property tax. According to a report in The Pointer, Tedjo won the mayoral race two weeks ago as a relative newcomer, defeating two veteran candidates, after previously spending four years as a councillor and making an earlier bid for mayor in a by-election. Athina Tagidou, president of the Applewood Heights Residents' Association, told The Pointer she believes residents' voices are often overlooked once politicians settle into long council careers, and said she has pushed for budget transparency through public consultations and calls for independent financial oversight. The report notes Tedjo's tax freeze promise has raised questions among residents about where the city will find savings, what spending could realistically be cut, and whether existing services and infrastructure can be maintained without simply delaying costs. The Pointer draws a comparison to Brampton Mayor Patrick Brown, who made a similar tax freeze pledge after his own surprise win in 2018 and has since faced criticism over his city's financial management. Tedjo's 2027 budget is expected to be the first real test of whether he can balance that promise against the city's ongoing financial needs.

items.title: Durham Health Officials Expand List of Measles Exposure Sites Tied to Pearson Airport
items.summary: Durham Region health officials say they have expanded the list of public exposure sites linked to a confirmed measles case involving an unimmunized child from the region who had recently travelled internationally. According to the Durham Region Health Department, anyone who passed through Toronto Pearson International Airport last week may have been exposed, along with people who visited the newly added locations. The department says it has already followed up directly with known contacts in Durham Region, and advises anyone who may have been exposed to watch for symptoms until Nov. 24. Health officials are urging residents to confirm they and their families have received two doses of the measles vaccine, noting that those born before 1970 likely had measles as children and are considered protected. Anyone who develops symptoms is advised to stay home from work or school, call ahead before visiting a doctor or clinic, and wear a well-fitting mask when seeking care, the health department says. Measles is highly contagious, officials note, and can linger in the air or on surfaces for up to two hours, with symptoms typically appearing seven to 21 days after exposure.

items.title: Brampton Man Faces Nine Charges After Three-Month Street Racing Investigation
items.summary: A Brampton man is facing nine charges following a three-month investigation into illegal street racing across Mississauga and Toronto. According to insauga.com, Peel Regional Police's Safer Roads Team identified a driver allegedly taking part in multiple illegal races while driving a vehicle with no licence plates and disguising his identity with a ski mask. The outlet reported officers spotted the same vehicle racing on two separate occasions on Sept. 26, once near Meadowpine Boulevard and Danbro Crescent, where police say the car ran a red light at Winston Churchill Boulevard and Highway 401, and again near Clayson Road and Bartor Road in Toronto. Police identified the driver as Tarman Toor, 24, of Brampton, insauga.com said. Officers executed a search warrant at a Brampton home on Oct. 28 and arrested Toor, according to the outlet. He is charged with three counts each of dangerous operation of a vehicle, disguise with intent and racing a motor vehicle, and is scheduled to appear in court in Brampton at a later date, insauga.com reported.
